name: Zedekiah
bio:
Mattaniah, son of Josiah and brother of Jehoahaz, was installed as king of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar after the deportation of his nephew Jehoiachin; Nebuchadnezzar renamed him Zedekiah. He began to reign at twenty-one and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; his mother was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. He did evil in the LORD's eyes like Jehoiakim before him, and eventually rebelled against Babylon, a decision driven, Scripture says, by the LORD's anger finally casting Judah from his presence (2 Kings 24:17-20).

## 📖 Core Story: The Fall of Jerusalem

In Zedekiah's ninth year, Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem; the siege lasted until famine gripped the city in his eleventh year. When the wall was finally breached, Zedekiah fled by night toward the plain but was captured near Jericho. Brought before Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, he watched his own sons executed before his eyes, then had his own eyes put out and was bound in bronze shackles and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:1-7). A month later, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, burned the temple, the palace, and all of Jerusalem, tore down its walls, and deported most of the surviving population, leaving only the poorest to work the land (2 Kings 25:8-12).

Chronicles frames his downfall in more explicitly theological terms: Zedekiah refused to humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, and the chief priests and the people joined him in defiling the temple with pagan practices. The LORD, out of compassion for his people, kept sending them messengers of warning, but they mocked God's messengers, scorned his words, and ridiculed his prophets until his wrath rose against them beyond remedy — bringing on the king of the Chaldeans, who showed no mercy to young or old. The exile that followed fulfilled the LORD's word through Jeremiah that the land would lie desolate and keep sabbath for seventy years (2 Chronicles 36:11-21).
